title: developer-platform-pilot-playbook-costing-and-security-pack-2028
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook helps platform engineers and solution teams run a short, high-impact pilot with Redwood Inference focused on developer ergonomics, predictable latency, and unit-cost validation. The document bundles positioning language, a competitive brief, a 6-week pilot plan, pricing guidance, a compact pitch outline for SEs, success metrics, a short customer case study vignette, and a security FAQ tailored to technical buyers.

Who this is for
- Platform engineers evaluating an LLM inference provider for productization.
- Solution engineers running pilot proofs-of-value for developer adoption.
- Procurement/security teams validating risk controls for production rollout.

Executive positioning (one-paragraph)
Redwood Inference offers a developer-first inference platform that abstracts away underlying GPU and network complexity while giving platform teams explicit controls to trade latency for unit cost. For teams that care about predictable production economics, compliance options, and fast developer onboarding, Redwood provides a consistent API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment models plus tooling to measure and control token-level cost. Use this playbook to demonstrate how Redwood reduces iteration time for developer teams while bounding inference spend.

Competitive brief (concise)
- Primary competitor profiles and how to position: 
  - Cloud-managed endpoints (e.g., large cloud provider managed model endpoints): emphasize Redwood's unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and transparent per-token economics vs opaque cloud egress/instance cost.
  - LLM API vendors (single-model, closed): emphasize Redwood's model catalog and model-variant fallbacks to preserve availability and quality.
  - Self-hosted runtimes (open-source + infra ops): emphasize Redwood's compile-time kernel selection, auto-batching heuristics, and production observability that reduce devops overhead and time-to-scale.

Key differentiators to call out in conversations
- Predictable unit economics: token-level cost breakdowns and per-route cost allocation.
- Unified API: Same interface and rollout controls across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Reliability fallbacks: automatic model-variant routing, region fallback and canary rollouts integrated into the control plane.
- Developer ergonomics: quickstart SDKs, structured output and streaming for interactive integrations.

6-week pilot plan (recommended timeline and milestones)
1) Week 0: Kickoff & Success Criteria (1 day)
   - Participants: platform eng, SE, product lead, security reviewer.
   - Output: signed pilot charter with KPIs (latency p50/p95 target, per-1000-token cost, dev onboarding time).
2) Week 1: Environment & Ingestion (3 days)
   - Provision Redwood test tenant (hosted) or private eval (VPC) depending on security needs.
   - Wire a representative sample API route and dataset (5–10 prompts or flows).
3) Week 2: Baseline Metrics & Profiling (5 days)
   - Run baseline traffic at representative concurrency; collect p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-cost breakdown.
   - Run profiling: sequence length distribution, tail-latency triggers, KV cache hit-rate.
4) Week 3: Optimization & Controls (5 days)
   - Enable prefix/KV caching, test batching policies, try quantized model variant.
   - Document latency vs cost trade-offs and recommended config for production.
5) Week 4: Reliability & Rollout Testing (4 days)
   - Configure canary rollout with fallback policy. Simulate capacity event and validate graceful degradation.
6) Week 5: Security Review & Compliance Checks (3 days)
   - Obtain evidence bundles: audit logs, KMS integration guide, network topology diagram.
7) Week 6: Wrap-up & Next Steps (3 days)
   - Present results: KPI dashboard, cost delta vs baseline, recommended deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), and proposal for 90-day production ramp.

Pilot success criteria (example KPIs)
- Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 450ms at target concurrency.
- Cost: incremental inference cost < $0.25 per 1K tokens after optimization (example target; adjust by workload).
- Developer time-to-first-API-call: < 2 hours for SDK quickstart.
- Reliability: automated fallback keeps error rate < 0.5% during induced fault test.
- Observability coverage: token-level cost and per-route latency traces available in console.

Pricing guidance (practical approach for pilots)
- Pilot pricing model options to offer prospects (pick one):
  1) Timeboxed credits: $X in hosted credit covering N tokens / 30 days.
  2) Metered pilot with reporting: standard per-token units with a capped monthly commit.
  3) Short-term Dedicated trial: discounted reserved capacity for a 6–8 week trial.
- Example cost projection (simple table):
  | Scenario | Avg tokens / req | Req/sec | Monthly Requests | Monthly tokens | Estimated cost (hosted) |
  |---------|-----------------|---------|------------------|----------------|------------------------|
  | Chat 1   | 600             | 1.2     | 3,110,400        | 1.86B          | $3,720                |
  | Embeddings | 512           | 0.2     | 518,400          | 265M           | $1,060                |
- Guidance: run with representative traces from production or staging traffic. Batching and caching recommendations often reduce cost by 25–65% depending on prompt reuse.

SE pitch deck outline (5 slides, one-line purpose each)
1) Problem (1 slide): inconsistent inference economics, noisy latency, fragmentation between hosted and private.
2) Solution (1 slide): Redwood’s unified runtime + controls that let dev teams predict cost and latency.
3) Pilot approach & success criteria (1 slide): 6-week plan, KPIs, and low-effort onboarding.
4) Economics & reliability proof points (1 slide): sample cost projection, fallback examples, SLOs met in prior customers.
5) Next steps & ask (1 slide): pilot activation, decision gates, and procurement timeline.

Customer vignette (short case study)
- Customer: Arbor Health (fictional synthesis to illustrate narrative).
- Problem: High variability in inference cost and slow model rollouts across internal teams.
- Pilot outcome (6 weeks): reduced median token cost by 38% through KV caching + selective quantized model variants; p95 latency improved by 22% after batching policy tweaks; developer time-to-first-call reduced from 2 days to 90 minutes with SDK templates.
- Business impact: estimated annualized inference savings of $180k for the initial product team, faster feature iteration leading to a 2-week speedup in release cadence.

Security FAQ (targeted for platform/security reviewers)
Q: What deployment models are available during a pilot?
A: Hosted (fastest) and Private VPC (customer-managed networking). For sensitive workloads we offer an on-prem package with air-gapped options; pilot can start hosted with a plan to migrate to private if required.

Q: How are keys and secrets managed?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers. For Private deployments the customer retains KMS control; Hosted uses per-tenant customer keys when requested.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and traceability?
A: Yes — token-level usage records, model/version metadata, and per-request traces are available via the Console and can be exported to SIEMs.

Q: What network controls exist for private deployments?
A: Private VPC deployments support customer-specified subnets, security groups, and private peering. We provide a network diagram and step-by-step connectivity checklist during onboarding.

Q: How is data residency handled in hosted mode?
A: Customers can select region-specific deployments; audit artifacts include data flow diagrams and retention policies. For strict residency requirements, we recommend Private deployments.

Onboarding checklist (compact)
- [ ] Pilot charter signed (KPIs and success criteria)
- [ ] Tenant provisioned (hosted or private)
- [ ] Sample prompt set and traces uploaded
- [ ] Initial baseline run completed and dashboard shared
- [ ] Optimization changes applied and retested
- [ ] Security evidence bundle submitted
- [ ] Final report with recommended next steps delivered

Runbooks & artifacts delivered with pilot
- Baseline performance dashboard (p50/p95, throughput, token-cost).
- Optimization notes: batching settings, cache TTLs, quantization profile used.
- Security evidence: network diagram, KMS integration guide, audit-log sample.
- Rollout recipe: canary steps and rollback triggers.

Appendix: sample curl quickstart (hosted)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-4b-optimized","input":"Summarize the following customer query...","stream":true}'

Notes on tailoring the playbook
- Replace sample token-cost estimates with actual traces for each prospect.
- For regulated customers, schedule the Private evaluation early (Week 0–1).
- Use the customer vignette to highlight economic and developer velocity outcomes rather than raw bench numbers.
